title: The Letters: Shapes Before Names
overview:
Hold a pen. Copy the 26 shapes.
Do not worry about the names yet. Names come in Unit 3.
Some shapes look the same. We look at those too.
functions: Hold a pen and make a line and a circle
Copy a letter shape from a model
Say if two shapes are the same or different
Tell b and d apart, and p and q
Write on a line, from left to right
Ask a person to show you again
learningPath: Words: the pen and the paper.
Patterns: lines, circles, and the line you write on.
Copy letters. Then copy your name.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 2. Today we use a pen.
You do not need the letter names today.
A letter is a shape. You can copy a shape.
Every letter is made of two things.
Lines and circles. That is all.
Look at l. That is one line.
Look at o. That is one circle.
Look at b. That is a line and a circle.
Now, English is written left to right.
Start on the left. Go to the right.
The letters sit on a line.
Some letters go under the line.
They are g, j, p, q and y.
Now the hard part. Some shapes look the same.
Look at b and d. The circle moves.
In b, the line is first. Then the circle.
In d, the circle is first. Then the line.
Look at p and q. It is the same problem.
Look at m and n. Count the humps.
m has two humps. n has one hump.
Do not hurry. Copy each shape slowly.
A slow letter you can read beats a fast one you cannot.

grammar.title: Every letter is lines and circles
grammar.explanation:
A letter looks hard.
It is not.
It is a line, a circle, or both.
grammar.rule:
Lines only:  l  i  t  v  x  z
Circles only:  o
Line and circle:  b  d  p  q  a
Humps:  m  n  h  r
grammar.workedExample:
You want to write b.
1. Look at it. b
2. Find the line. It is on the left.
3. Draw the line down.
4. Find the circle. It is on the right.
5. Draw it. You have b.
grammar.mistake:
Do not draw the whole letter in one go.
Draw the line. Then draw the circle.
Two small moves beat one big one.
grammar.tip: Line first, circle second. For b and p.
grammar.practice:
Which is it: line, circle, or both?
1. o
2. l
3. d
4. i
5. p
6. m
grammar.answers:
1. circle
2. line
3. both
4. line
5. both
6. lines and humps
Five or six right? You can see how a letter is made.

grammar.title: The line, and what sits under it
grammar.explanation:
Letters sit on a line.
Most letters stay on top.
Five letters go under it.
grammar.rule:
On the line:  a  c  e  m  n  o  s
Tall, above:  b  d  h  k  l  t
Under the line:  g  j  p  q  y
grammar.workedExample:
You write the word page.
1. p goes under the line.
2. a sits on the line.
3. g goes under the line.
4. e sits on the line.
5. Check: two letters under.
grammar.mistake:
A letter floating above the line is hard to read.
Put every letter on the line first.
Then let g, j, p, q and y drop.
grammar.tip: Five letters go under: g, j, p, q, y.
grammar.practice:
Does it go under the line? Yes or no.
1. p
2. a
3. g
4. m
5. y
6. o
grammar.answers:
1. yes
2. no
3. yes
4. no
5. yes
6. no
All six right? Your writing will sit straight.

grammar.title: b and d, p and q
grammar.explanation:
These four shapes are the same shape.
Only the side changes.
Every learner finds this hard. It is normal.
grammar.rule:
b:  line, then circle on the right
d:  circle, then line on the right
p:  line down under, circle on the right
q:  circle, then line down under

bed  -  the b looks left, the d looks right
grammar.workedExample:
You see a letter. Is it b or d?
1. Find the circle.
2. Is the line before it?
3. Yes? It is b.
4. No, the circle is first? It is d.
5. Check with the word bed.
grammar.mistake:
Do not guess from the name.
Look at the order: line first, or circle first.
The word bed helps every time.
grammar.tip: b comes before d in the alphabet.
grammar.practice:
b or d?
1. The first letter of bag.
2. The first letter of door.
3. The last letter of bed.
4. The first letter of bed.
5. The first letter of day.
grammar.answers:
1. b
2. d
3. d
4. b
5. d
Wrong on any? Write the word bed. Look at it. Try again.

grammar.title: Same or different?
grammar.explanation:
Before you read, you must see.
Two shapes: are they the same?
This is the first reading skill.
grammar.rule:
Same:      b  b       o  o       m  m
Different: b  d       o  c       m  n

Look at the whole shape.
Then look at the parts.
grammar.workedExample:
You see: p  q
1. Both have a circle and a line.
2. Where is the circle in the first?
3. On the right.
4. Where in the second? On the left.
5. So they are different.
grammar.mistake:
A quick look says they are the same.
A slow look finds the difference.
Slow is right here.
grammar.tip: Look at the side the circle is on.
grammar.practice:
Same or different?
1. n  n
2. m  n
3. c  c
4. p  q
5. o  o
6. b  b
grammar.answers:
1. same
2. different
3. same
4. different
5. same
6. same
All six? You are ready for letter names in Unit 3.

readings.title: My First Page
readings.setting: At a table, with a pen and paper
readings.passage:
This is my pen.
This is my paper.
I draw a line.
I draw a circle.
Now I copy a letter.
I copy b. Line first, then circle.
I copy d. Circle first, then line.
They are different.
I can see it now.

readings.title: Two Humps and One
readings.genre: A short text about m and n
readings.setting: A classroom, looking at a word list
readings.passage:
Look at m.
Count the humps. One, two.
m has two humps.
Now look at n.
Count the humps. One.
n has one hump.
The word name has both.
n first, then m.
Say it slowly: n-a-m-e.

readings.title: How to Write on This Page
readings.setting: A wall in an adult class
readings.passage:
Write on the line.
Start on the left.
Go to the right.
g, j, p, q and y go under the line.
Do not hurry.
A slow letter is a good letter.

comprehension.q: What does the writer draw first?

comprehension.why: Line 6: I copy b. Line first, then circle.
Line 7: I copy d. Circle first, then line.

comprehension.q: Can the writer tell b and d apart now?
comprehension.why: The last line: I can see it now.

comprehension.q: Which letter comes first in name?
Which five letters go under the line?
comprehension.a: g, j, p, q and y.

comprehension.q: Why does the notice say do not hurry?
comprehension.a: Because a slow letter is easier to read.
comprehension.why: The last line: A slow letter is a good letter.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Line, circle, or both?
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. You will hear a letter.
Say: line, circle, or both.
1. o
2. l
3. b
4. i
5. d
6. t
Tap the mic. Say your six answers.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: 1 circle, 2 line, 3 both, 4 line, 5 both, 6 line.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name a letter. Say what it is made of.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Say the shape, not the name
speaking.instructions:
Look at a letter. Do not say its name.
Say what it is made of.
Like this: a line, and a circle on the right.
Do it for b, d, m, n and o.
Tap the mic. Say five descriptions.
Tap again. Listen back.
speaking.tutor: Describe a letter to the tutor without its name. Ask it to guess.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Same or different?
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. You will hear two letters.
Say same or different.
1. b, b
2. m, n
3. o, o
4. p, q
5. d, d
6. b, d
Tap the mic. Say six answers.
Check: 1 same, 2 different, 3 same, 4 different, 5 same, 6 different.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for two letters. Say if they are the same.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Ask to see it again
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: This is b. B: Sorry? Show me again.
2. A: Write it here. B: Here? On this line?
3. A: Yes. B: Thank you.
4. A: Now copy it. B: Slowly, please.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Tap again. Listen.
Check: did you ask, not just wait?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to show you a letter again. Use: Show me again, please.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Count the humps
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Count the humps.
1. m
2. n
3. m
4. n
5. m
Say a number for each one.
Tap the mic. Say five numbers.
Check: 2, 1, 2, 1, 2.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say m or n. Say how many humps you heard.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Saying b and d out loud
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
b  b  b
d  d  d
For b, your lips close. Feel it.
For d, your tongue goes up. Feel it.
Now say these.
bed
bad
dad
did
Tap the mic. Say the four words.
Check: can you hear the b and the d?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say bed and dad. Say which starts with b.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Lines and circles
writing.prompt:
Fill one line with straight lines.
Fill one line with circles.
Do not write letters yet.
writing.model:
| | | | | | | | | |
o o o o o o o o o o
writing.criteria:
Ten lines on the first row.
Ten circles on the second.
The lines are straight.
The circles are closed.
writing.support: Do five of each. Rest. Then do five more.
writing.extension: Now make the circles all the same size.

writing.title: Writing 2 — Copy all 26 letters
writing.prompt:
Copy every small letter.
Look at the model. Copy one letter.
Check it. Then the next.
writing.model:
a b c d e f g
h i j k l m n
o p q r s t u
v w x y z
writing.criteria:
All 26 letters.
In the right order.
Each one on the line.
writing.support: Do a to g today. Do the rest tomorrow.
writing.extension: Now write the capitals: A B C.

writing.title: Writing 3 — The four hard ones
writing.prompt:
Write b, d, p and q.
Write each one four times.
Say the order out loud as you write.
writing.model:
b b b b
d d d d
p p p p
q q q q
writing.criteria:
Sixteen letters.
p and q go under the line.
b and d stay on the line.
You can tell them apart.
writing.support: Write b and d only. Add p and q later.
writing.extension: Now write the word bed. Then the word dad.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Your hand and the pen
activities.instructions:
1. Hold the pen between your thumb and two fingers.
2. Rest your hand on the paper.
3. Draw one long line.
4. Draw one circle.
5. Is your hand tired? Rest.
6. Do it again.
activities.answers:
There is no right answer here.
Check: is the line straight?
Is the circle closed?
Is your hand resting on the paper, not floating?
activities.solo: Do it alone. Then look at your page.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Copy the letter
activities.instructions:
Copy each letter three times.
1. a
2. o
3. b
4. d
5. m
6. n
7. p
8. q
9. l
10. t
activities.answers:
There is no key. Check your own page.
Is each copy like the model?
Eight or more good copies: go on.
Below eight: do five letters only, slowly.
activities.solo: Copy first. Then compare with the model.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Same or different?
activities.instructions:
Write same or different.
1. b  b
2. b  d
3. o  o
4. m  n
5. p  p
6. p  q
7. n  n
8. d  b
9. a  a
10. q  p
activities.answers:
1. same
2. different
3. same
4. different
5. same
6. different
7. same
8. different
9. same
10. different
Eight or more right: good.
Below eight: look at the circle's side.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Which one is it?
activities.instructions:
Look and choose.
1. The first letter of bag: b or d?
2. The first letter of door: b or d?
3. The first letter of pen: p or q?
4. The first letter of map: m or n?
5. The first letter of name: m or n?
6. The last letter of bed: b or d?
activities.answers:
1. b
2. d
3. p
4. m
5. n
6. d
Five or six right: good.
Below five: read Pattern 3 again.

activities.title: Practice 5 — On the line or under it?
activities.instructions:
Write on or under.
1. a
2. p
3. m
4. g
5. o
6. y
7. n
8. j
activities.answers:
1. on
2. under
3. on
4. under
5. on
6. under
7. on
8. under
Seven or eight right: your writing will sit straight.
activities.solo: Say each answer out loud, then check.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Find the letter
activities.instructions:
Look at this line of letters.
b  d  o  m  b  n  p  d  b  q
1. How many b are there?
2. How many d are there?
3. Is there a q?
4. Point to the first m.
5. Point to the last letter.
activities.answers:
1. Three
2. Two
3. Yes, one, at the end
4. It is the fourth letter
5. The last letter is q
Four or five right: you can find a shape in a line. That is reading.
activities.solo: Point with your finger as you count.

quizzes.q: Which letter is a circle only?
quizzes.why: o is one circle. l is one line. b has both.

quizzes.q: In the letter b, the ___ comes first.
quizzes.why: b is the line, then the circle. In d the circle is first.

quizzes.q: In the letter d, the ___ comes first.
quizzes.why: d is the circle, then the line on the right.
m has two humps. n has one.
n has one hump. m has two.

quizzes.q: Which letter goes under the line?
quizzes.why: Five letters go under: g, j, p, q and y.
The other three pairs look alike but are different letters.

quizzes.q: In English you start writing on the ___.
You did not see the shape. What do you say?
quizzes.why: Asking is faster than guessing. The others do not ask.

options: The big form of a letter
quizzes.a: The big form of a letter
quizzes.why: A is capital. a is small.

quizzes.q: Which is the small form of B?
quizzes.why: b is small. d is a different letter.

quizzes.q: Which word helps you remember b and d?
quizzes.why: In bed, the b looks left. The d looks right.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example before its practice, every practice has an answer key, and every writing task has a model to copy. Sit beside rather than lead.

An adult who has never written this script has two problems: making the shape, and knowing what it is called. Teaching both at once is what makes the alphabet feel impossible. This unit is hands only. Names come in Unit 3. Do not name the letters here even if the learner asks — tell them the name is coming next.

teacherNotes.type: b and d is not a reading problem
teacherNotes.note: Every learner of this script confuses them, including children who have read for years. It is a visual problem, not a sign of difficulty. Say so out loud: it will save a learner from deciding they cannot do this.

teacherNotes.type: Watch the hand, not the page
teacherNotes.note: A tired grip makes bad letters and the learner blames themselves. Look for a white thumb or a hand floating off the paper, and stop for a rest before the page gets worse.
A left-handed learner covers what they have just written and may hook their wrist. Turn the paper clockwise about 30 degrees and the hook usually goes.

selfAssessment.statement: I can hold a pen and draw a line.
I can copy any letter from a model.
I can see if two letters are the same.
I can tell b from d, and p from q.
I can write on a line, from left to right.
I can ask a person to show me again.

assignment.title: Copy the letters, and the four hard ones
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Copy all 26 small letters on lines.
2. Write b, d, p and q four times each.
Then write the word bed.
Check your page before you finish.
